column1: # Server-binding requirements that no black-box case checks, and why. Every server-binding requirement
# in requirements.tsv is either cited by a case or listed here (a unit test enforces both directions).
# category: not-black-box   no externally observable server behaviour distinguishes compliance
#           needs-capability  checkable only with a broker feature or setup the suite cannot provide
#                             generically (enhanced-auth mechanism, bridging, restart, admin API)
#           informative       MAY / SHOULD statements the suite deliberately does not assert

column3: reason
Retained messages surviving a restart needs the broker restarted on the same storage; the suite cannot restart an arbitrary broker.
QoS 0 messages are never stored is descriptive prose in 3.1 §2.2, not a requirement; a stored QoS 0 message is noted (persistence/qos0_messages_queued_while_offline_are_noted).
MAY: an administrative mechanism to delete stored sessions is optional and outside MQTT.
Client-side SHOULD about reserved CONNECT flag bit 0; a 3.1 server may accept or reject it, so both behaviours conform.
The CONNECT timeout is configurable and its value unspecified, so no observable deadline can be asserted.
MAY: delivering before SUBACK; the harness accepts either order.
MAY: granting a lower QoS; downgrade cases accept any granted QoS up to the requested one.
MAY: sender-side retry with DUP; the server accepting DUP retries is checked elsewhere.
The retry timeout policy is configurable and unspecified.
SHOULD: in-session retry timing is unspecified; redelivery on reconnect is asserted under V31-4.2-3.
MAY: 3.1 defines no special $ topics; applying the 3.1.1 rule is optional.
A topic over 65535 bytes cannot be encoded in the 2-byte length prefix, so no server behaviour differs.
A transient server-side processing error cannot be induced from outside the broker.
Bridge (outbound client) conformance needs a bridge configured to a second broker.
A reordered CONNECT payload parses as different but valid field values, so no server behaviour distinguishes it.
Needs authentication or authorization configured so that a check can fail; an anonymous broker performs none.
Transport requirement trivially met: every case runs over TCP.
A topic over 65,535 bytes cannot be encoded in the 2-byte length prefix, so no server behaviour differs.
Client rule during an enhanced-auth exchange; observable only on a broker offering an Authentication Method.
The server sends AUTH only during enhanced authentication, which needs a broker offering an Authentication Method.
Server-sent AUTH exists only during enhanced authentication.
Server-sent AUTH exists only during enhanced authentication.
An AUTH 0x18 challenge needs a broker offering an Authentication Method; mechanisms are broker-specific.
Client response to a server AUTH challenge; needs an enhanced-auth broker.
Rejection during an AUTH exchange needs an enhanced-auth broker (an unknown method is MQTT-4.12.0-1, checked).
The same Authentication Method on AUTH and CONNACK only exists after a successful enhanced authentication.
Re-authentication needs a broker that offers an Authentication Method.
Failed re-authentication needs a broker that offers an Authentication Method.
MAY: a 3.1 server may delete a retained message on a zero-length retained PUBLISH; deletion is mandatory only from 3.1.1.
